summary: The core is built as a netlist of the board's own chips, named by board location (U2A/U2B 74107 clock dividers, U9R 74138 H-decoder, U12P/U12U/U10N/U10P sprite latches, U11H/U12H 161 counters, 2511 alternating sprite line buffers, 4 background ROM shifters with preset counters). Sprites are drawn by a scan-time pipeline that walks sprite RAM with a counter, compares Y against the raster with an adder, and writes pixels into V0-alternating line buffers through up/down address counters. MAME does this per frame with gfx->transmask and per-scanline loops. The only part that echoes MAME is the AY port-A ^0x40 protection toggle.

findings.where: rtl/excore.v (U2A_A/U2A_B/U2B_A ls107, U9R ls138x, U6N_VRAM, U4N_Z80A_RAM, U11SR, UL8, UE1, U10H)
findings.note: Each instance and latch is named for a chip position and implemented as that chip type (74107 JK flops, 74138 decoder, 6116/2114/2511 RAMs, 6301/6331 PROMs), with chip-style ports.

findings.signal: clocks from JK flip-flop divider chain
findings.note: The 10 MHz, 6.66 MHz and 3.33 MHz video clocks come from cascaded ls107 flip-flops clocked by 20 MHz, i.e. the board's divider, rather than an abstract pixel-clock enable.

findings.signal: scan-time sprite engine with phase strobes P[4:1]
findings.note: Sprite RAM is walked by a counter (spramaddr_cnt). Phase strobes decoded from its low bits clock the latches U12P, U12U, U12L, U10N and U10P. The Y match uses an adder (U12_sum = sprite Y + V + 1), and the 161 counters U11H/U12H feed XOR flip gates. MAME instead loops over spriteram calling gfx->transmask.

findings.signal: alternating line buffers with up/down load counters
findings.note: Two m2511 4-bit line buffers swap on rpixelbusV[0]. Their write and clock strobes are gated from 10 MHz and flip-flop outputs (U9H, U9F), and their addresses come from loadable up/down counters preset from the sprite X byte (191-style), which is board structure.

VRAM is addressed by the flipped H/V counter bits. The tile byte is latched on negedge pixH[2], the char ROM output is latched on pixH[1], and a 4:1 mux on H[1:0] picks the pixel feeding PROM L8, all clocked by raster bits like the board.

findings.signal: background latch strobes via decoder and preset counters
findings.note: A 1-of-13 decode (SLD/CDCK) of the sub-CPU address strobes individual ROM-address and start/stop latches. Four preset counters and 2-bit pixel muxes feed PROMs 4KJ and 3L. MAME holds m_background_latches[13] in an array and loops per scanline over x.

findings.signal: SNHI/VDSP derived from H counter decode
findings.note: The sub CPU reads SNHI and VDSP, which are generated from pixH[8:6] and the blanking registers. It also gates a 7474 (U8T_B) with them, where MAME computes the same values from screen->hpos().

findings.signal: diverges from MAME's PC-based protection hack
findings.note: There is no protection_r equivalent that checks PC 0x4143 and reads ROM at 0x33c0. The 6000-7FFF range is plain work RAM, which is how the board would decode it.
The AY2 port A input is a register toggled with ^8'h40 and seeded from port B. This copies MAME's porta_r ^0x40 trick, not a modelled circuit, although it seeds from IOB rather than from ROM 0x5f76.
Text over sprites over background, selected by non-zero pixel. This matches MAME's draw order but is also what a priority circuit gives. The colour comes straight from PROM E1.
The address decode matches MAME's maps, as any correct core must.
